answer: Ferrous-Tide Attestation Credits. Each identity must hold credits earned only through sustained participation in resource-limited physical sites, such as karst aquifer monitoring stations. Credits decay with a fixed half-life and are non-transferable, so a new identity cannot be bought into standing. The flood tide of registrations resets an attacker's decay clock, forcing repeated on-site work. Cost per identity is measured in verified labor-hours at scarce sites, not money.
